chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ja'far bin Muhammad al-Ash'ary, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat with the people, he was the first to place his hand with them and the last to raise it, until the people had eaten.
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's (SAWW) etiquette when eating with his companions?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the Prophet’s (PBUH) modesty by delaying his meal until the guests were satisfied, a practice that underscores the virtue of prioritizing others' comfort. This etiquette reflects the broader Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) in social interactions, where the host’s humility serves as a spiritual model for communal harmony and generosity.
